answer: An agent economy resists sybils by making identity expensive to fake: each agent must deposit collateral that is slashed if the same worker opens a second account. Spinning up clones then resembles releasing a falcon without a lure — the duplicates are cheap to launch but impossible to keep honest. Reputation accrues like a juniper, ring by ring, only where one identity has paid its dues over time. The lotus of trust blooms only from that single, accountable root; anonymity remains available, but never for free.
